jobs.description: Job Description Position Summary The Senior Analyst, Replenishment Logistics supports end-to-end basing logistics planning and execution by coordinating schedules, daily operations, and recovery plans across replenishment, warehousing, fulfillment, damage prevention, and customer management. This role translates planning signals into actionable operating plans, monitors execution to service and cost targets, identifies risks and constraints, and drives cross-functional actions to stabilize performance and drive predictability. serves as a subject matter expert for ocean network operations, leading complex analyses, driving strategic improvement initiatives, identifying operational risks and opportunities, and recommending solutions that enhance cost, service, and network performance. This role partners closely with Brewery and Winery Operations, Supply Chain Planning, Fulfillment, Distributor Operations, Customer Management, and domestic and international logistics partners to ensure reliable product flow and operational excellence across the global supply chain Specialty Focus: This role is responsible for coordinating, communicating, executing transportation plans and supporting operations execution, and for tracking carrier and vendor performance metrics related to cost, transit time, velocity, and working capital management. The analyst services internal and external stakeholders by preparing performance insights, facilitating decision-making, and driving follow-up actions through S&OP, S&OE, Brewery & Winery Replenishment, and Distributor Operations Management. Core Responsibilities: Operations Analyst (≈80%) Execution & Operating Routines Coordinates basing logistics plans and operating schedules (daily/weekly/monthly) across replenishment, warehouse, and fulfillment to meet service, cost, and inventory targets, including support for appointment scheduling and shipment execution alignment Monitors execution versus plan; identifies constraints and execution gaps (e.g. MSO to target, appointment availability, late pickups, capacity, labor, inventory availability, carrier coverage) and drives same-day/week recovery actions with functional owners. Prepares agendas, pre-reads, and action logs for S&OE/weekly execution reviews, Distributor Operations touchpoints, and site/warehouse operating reviews, ensuring alignment on shipment execution, service risks, and recovery actions, and documents decisions and follow-ups. Leads issue triage by gathering facts, quantifying customer/service impact, and routing/owning actions across replenishment, fulfillment, damage prevention, transportation, and customer management teams through to closure. Reporting & Data Support Builds and maintains routine performance reporting (service, fill rate, on-time delivery, inventory health, damages, claims, transportation cost, transit time, velocity, and working capital) using available system outputs, platforms, and business intelligence tools to deliver accurate, timely, and standardized insights. Validates data completeness and investigates anomalies; partners with WMS/TMS/ERP process owners, carriers, and vendors to correct data and address root causes impacting metrics and execution performance. Compiles weekly and monthly KPI packs and scorecards for S&OP, S&OE, Distributor Operations, and Logistics Council forums; ensures consistent metric definitions, commentary, and version control, and highlights key risks, gaps, and performance trends. Documentation & Training Support Maintains operations playbooks and documentation (standard work, escalation paths, recovery plans, capacity assumptions, carrier routing guides, and hand-offs) by incorporating approved changes and confirming owners and effective dates. Supports deployment of new routines and changes by preparing materials, coordinating communications, and tracking completion/adoption across internal teams and external partners as needed. Ensures operating standards, scheduling expectations, and escalation processes are communicated consistently across replenishment, warehousing, fulfillment, transportation partners, and customer-facing teams. Contributes to, creates and maintains standard operating procedures, process/decision flow maps, and best practice documentation. Cross-Functional Coordination Coordinates across Logistics, Customer Management, Supply Chain Planning, Warehouse Operations, Procurement, Finance, and IT—plus carriers and 3PLs—to align capacity, resolve execution issues, and close action items. Drafts clear updates on transportation plans, exceptions, and recovery actions; facilitates timely escalation and decision-making to protect customer commitments and cost targets. Ability to proactively communicate and matrix influence across internal and external stakeholders Role-Specific Responsibilities: (≈20%) Leads ocean network planning and execution in alignment with basing plans, inventory requirements, warehouse capacity, and customer service expectations; identifies risks, constraints, and optimization opportunities. Owns ocean network performance management, analyzing transportation cost, transit time reliability, container velocity, dwell time, service performance, claims/damages, and working capital drivers; develops recommendations and drives corrective actions. Leads management of ocean network exceptions, including vessel delays, port congestion, customs holds, equipment shortages, drayage constraints, shortages, and damages; coordinates recovery efforts to minimize service and financial impacts. Drives continuous improvement initiatives by leveraging operational and financial data to improve service, inventory flow, network reliability, and total transportation cost; leads root cause analysis and corrective actions. Develops business insights, recommendations, and executive-ready materials for S&OP, S&OE, Distributor Operations, Logistics Council, and leadership reviews; translates network performance and risks into actionable decisions. Leads engagement with ocean network partners through performance reviews, capacity planning discussions, and corrective action follow-ups; drives accountability for service, cost, and operational performance. Supports transportation budgeting, forecasting, and financial planning by identifying cost trends, risks, savings opportunities, and network optimization initiatives. Leads cross-functional projects focused on ocean network optimization, cost reduction, service improvement, and process standardization; drives alignment and delivers measurable results. Supports ocean network risk management and contingency planning by evaluating routing alternatives, capacity strategies, and response plans for weather, port congestion, labor disruptions, and other supply chain risks. Minimum Qualifications (Core) Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience. Demonstrated ability to manage multiple priorities, maintain action logs, and drive closure across cross-functional teams in a fast-paced operating environment. Proficient in data analysis and interpretation; comfortable working with outputs from ERP/WMS/TMS and shipment visibility tools to build KPI reporting and insights. Strong written and verbal communication skills; able to translate data into clear narratives, facilitate operating routines, and escalate risks with recommended actions. Bilingual proficiency in English and Spanish is required, including the ability to communicate effectively both verbally and written Preferred Qualifications Experience coordinating transportation planning/execution and/or carrier performance management (scorecards, QBR support, corrective actions). Working knowledge of end-to-end supply chain processes (replenishment planning, warehousing, fulfillment, transportation, claims/damages, Distributor/Customs) and common system transactions. Job Overview
We are looking for an Mobile Security Specialist to establish and lead mobile security across the company, covering consumer-facing applications as well as seller, rider and logistics mobile products.
This will initially be a highly hands-on senior IC role. The person will be expected to understand the mobile threat landscape, identify systemic risks, build scalable security processes, and influence senior engineering leaders to improve the security posture of mobile applications across multiple organizations.

Mobile Threat Landscape and Strategy
Build and maintain a comprehensive view of mobile threats, attack paths and systemic control gaps across the company's mobile estate.
Define the target mobile security posture, priorities and longer-term roadmap.
Track relevant changes in iOS, Android and mobile exploitation techniques and translate them into concrete security requirements.
Security Architecture and Standards
Define practical security standards for iOS and Android, including application integrity, device trust, authentication, credential protection, local data, WebViews, deep links and third-party SDKs.
Identify recurring weaknesses across applications and drive platform-level solutions rather than repeated app-specific fixes.
Provide senior technical judgement on complex vulnerabilities, incidents and architectural decisions.
Security Assessment and Review Program
Build a repeatable, evidence-based process for assessing mobile application security.
Own and run the mobile security review program, including methodology, prioritization, acceptance criteria and escalation.
Improve the program over time through automation, engineering self-service and better measurement of security coverage and residual risk.
Cross-Organization Influence
Act as an agent of change for mobile security across engineering teams.
Work directly with Senior Directors, Principal Engineers and senior mobile leaders to influence architecture, engineering practices and investment priorities.
Drive security improvements across organizational boundaries without relying on formal authority.
Function Building and Leadership
Start as a deeply hands-on technical leader, working directly with applications, code, devices and security controls where required.
Establish the operating model for mobile security and identify where additional specialist capability is needed.
Over time, help build and manage a small specialist mobile security team.

Deep hands-on mobile security expertise across both iOS and Android, ideally developed in a large-scale consumer technology environment.
Strong practical experience in areas such as mobile application security, reverse engineering, app integrity, device trust, authentication, secure storage, IPC, WebViews, deep links, networking and abuse resistance.
Experience building or running a mobile security assessment or review program, rather than only performing individual reviews.
Strong software engineering background, ideally including production mobile development or development of mobile security tooling.
Demonstrated ability to identify systemic issues across multiple applications and translate them into reusable platform controls, standards or engineering frameworks.
Proven experience influencing senior engineers and engineering leaders across organizational boundaries.
Experience with product security architecture and threat modelling at significant scale.
Evidence of driving changes in engineering practice, not only identifying security issues.

This organization oversees all global middle and last mile products, spanning B2B and B2C, critical partners, enterprise and SMB customers across numerous teams. This includes—but is not limited to—Amazon Supply Chain Services, Amazon Freight, Amazon Relay, Amazon Freight Partners, Amazon Shipping, Amazon Flex, Amazon Hub Delivery and more. Everything we do is aimed at further delighting our shippers, carriers and partners with faster, cheaper, and more efficient means of shipping and receiving packages. Brand Experience (BEX) is a central shared-services creative studio supporting the portfolio of global supply chain products. The team develops brand strategy and creative solutions that engage global transportation audiences through the human stories behind logistics. We build and own the global brands and their creative expression throughout the customer journey—working closely with marketing, sales, and customer insights partners to test, learn, and ensure our design solutions resonate with target audiences. We have high standards and strive to continuously raise the bar across all creative elements. We are looking for a Senior Creative Program Manager to own resource management, capacity planning, and creative operations for a team of 25+ creatives (designers, copywriters, production artists, and more) supporting 10+ global businesses. This is a high-impact IC role at the center of how BEX operates—responsible for the systems, processes, and partnerships that enable our studio to deliver excellent creative work at scale. The right candidate brings deep expertise in creative program management and uses sound judgment to design long-term operational solutions in an environment where strategy is not always defined. They own complex, cross-functional programs end-to-end, create scalable mechanisms that increase studio efficiency, and influence across partner teams and senior leadership to drive alignment. They are both tactical and strategic—equally comfortable triaging today's incoming requests and building the capacity model for next quarter. They develop a strong understanding of Amazon's supply chain products and become the operational backbone of BEX, connecting the dots between business demand, creative capacity, and team health. This role partners closely with senior leadership on planning, goal development, and resource strategy. The Senior Creative Program Manager may manage contractor project managers in the future. Key job responsibilities Resource Management & Capacity Planning Own end-to-end resource management and capacity planning for the studio, mapping creative skills and availability against a portfolio of programs across 10+ global businesses Maintain workload balance across all studio members, strategically assigning projects to internal and external resources to optimize the pipeline and mitigate long-term risks Build and maintain forecasting models that anticipate demand, identify resourcing gaps, and inform headcount and vendor recommendations to leadership Make trade-offs between short-term delivery needs and long-term team sustainability, escalating appropriately when constraints require senior input Creative Operations & Process Own the studio's project management platform (Workfront), ensuring it serves as a reliable source of truth for project status, resource allocation, and reporting. Triage and traffic all new creative requests submitted to the studio, assessing scope, identifying information gaps, and determining owners and next steps Own and evolve creative development processes end-to-end (concept to production) across mediums including video, digital, social, OOH, direct mail, events, and sales collateral—ensuring on-time, on-budget delivery Design, document, and implement scalable mechanisms that systematically improve studio efficiency, throughput, and quality of output Drive operational excellence best practices across the studio; identify where to simplify, automate, or extend solutions for the best outcome Program Reporting & Studio Health Own, develop and maintain studio health dashboards that provide visibility into capacity utilization, delivery performance, and pipeline forecasting Develop program reporting across finance, business reviews, client satisfaction, and team goals—connecting operational metrics to org-level objectives Contribute to OP1/OP2 narratives and organizational goal-setting as they relate to creative operations and resource strategy Stakeholder Management & Communication Serve as a primary operational point of contact for Creative Garage, building effective partnerships with both the internal creative team and business partners across the global supply chain org Drive cross-functional alignment across multiple business partners and external agencies globally; educate partners on studio process, SLAs, and capacity constraints Anticipate bottlenecks, manage escalations, and balance business needs against resource constraints—finding a path forward in difficult situations Present updates to stakeholders and cross-functional partners, including senior management up to VP level, with clear and concise written and verbal communication Own change management communications for studio operations updates across creative team and business stakeholders About the team We call ourselves the Brand Experience. We are an internal creative studio built to centrally support the global supply chain org. We believe creatives working together on a central team creates a stronger, more collaborative environment—more career growth opportunities and stronger creative solutions for our customers. We make logistics human and love telling the stories of those who make the supply chain work. Most importantly, we make great creative and have fun doing it. Come build with us.
